sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was effectively lowered: the 777-9 first delivery was pushed to 2025 (from a prior expectation), and the 777-9 production rate ramp is being adjusted with a temporary pause through 2023, incurring ~$1.5 billion in abnormal costs. Additionally, the company recorded significant charges on fixed-price defense development programs (VC-25B $660M, T-7A $367M) and $212M for impacts of the war in Ukraine. While management expressed confidence in generating positive cash flow for 2022, the structural risks from certification delays, production pauses, and defense program charges outweigh the positive cash flow outlook, leading to a bearish signal.

summary.revenue: $14.0 billion, down 8% from $15.2 billion in Q1 2021, driven by lower defense volume and charges on fixed-price defense development programs, partially offset by commercial services volume.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($2.06) and core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($2.75). The GAAP loss per share was ($2.06) compared to ($0.92) in Q1 2021.
summary.guidance: The company continues to expect positive cash flow for 2022. 737 production rate expected to increase to 31 airplanes per month during Q2 2022. 777-9 first delivery now expected in 2025. 777-9 production rate ramp adjusted, including a temporary pause through 2023. 787 deliveries resume timing not specified, with gradual return to five per month over time. 777-8 Freighter first delivery anticipated in 2025.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin was (8.4)% compared to (0.5)% in Q1 2021. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) was (10.4)% compared to (2.3)% in Q1 2021. Commercial Airplanes operating margin was (20.6)%. Defense, Space & Security operating margin was (16.9)%. Global Services operating margin was 14.6%.
key_risks: Charges on fixed-price defense development programs: VC-25B $660 million charge, T-7A Red Hawk $367 million charge.
Impacts of the war in Ukraine: $212 million pre-tax charges.
777-9 certification delays: first delivery now expected in 2025, production rate ramp adjusted with temporary pause through 2023, resulting in ~$1.5 billion abnormal costs.
787 certification plan submitted to FAA but delivery resumption timing not specified; program producing at very low rate until deliveries resume.
Abnormal costs on 787 program of approximately $2 billion, most by end of 2023, including $312 million in the quarter.
Supply chain constraints, COVID-19, and inflationary pressures impacting supplier negotiations on T-7A program.
key_opportunities: 737 production and deliveries continue to increase; production rate expected to increase to 31 per month in Q2 2022.
Launched 777-8 Freighter with order from Qatar Airways.
Global Services revenue increased 15% and operating margin increased to 14.6% driven by higher commercial volume and favorable mix.
Total backlog of $371 billion, including nearly 4,200 commercial airplanes valued at $291 billion.
Company continues to expect positive cash flow for 2022.

management_tone.label: mixed
